decls.name: TauCeti.IsPrimitive
decls.doc:
A homology class `v : M` on a boundary torus is **primitive** when some `ℤ`-linear functional
`M →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ` sends it to `1`, so the span of `v` splits off a copy of `ℤ`. Over the standard
lattice `ℤ × ℤ` this is coprimality of the two coordinates (`TauCeti.isPrimitive_prod_iff`). The
definition mentions no basis, so it is preserved by every `ℤ`-linear equivalence
(`TauCeti.isPrimitive_congr`).
decls.statement: def IsPrimitive (v : M) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPrimitive.neg
decls.doc: Primitivity is unchanged by the sign action `v ↦ -v`.
decls.statement: theorem IsPrimitive.neg {v : M} (h : IsPrimitive v) : IsPrimitive (-v)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_congr
decls.doc: Primitivity transports along a `ℤ`-linear equivalence: it is a basis-free property.
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_congr (φ : M ≃ₗ[ℤ] N) {v : M} : IsPrimitive (φ v) ↔ IsPrimitive v

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeSetoid
decls.doc:
Two primitive classes represent the same slope when they agree up to sign. This is an
equivalence relation on primitive classes.
decls.statement:
def slopeSetoid (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] :
    Setoid {v : M // IsPrimitive v}

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeSetoid_rel_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of the relation defining slopes: representatives agree up to sign. This is
internal to the quotient construction; consumers use `Slope.mk_eq_mk_iff`.
decls.statement:
theorem slopeSetoid_rel_iff {a b : {v : M // IsPrimitive v}} :
    slopeSetoid M a b ↔ a.1 = b.1 ∨ a.1 = -b.1

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope
decls.doc:
A **slope** on a boundary torus with homology `M`: a primitive homology class taken modulo the
sign action, i.e. an unoriented essential simple closed curve up to isotopy. This is basis-free — it
refers only to the abstract module `M`, not to any choice of meridian-longitude basis.
decls.statement: def Slope (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.mk
decls.doc: The slope represented by a primitive class `v : M`.
decls.statement: def mk (v : M) (h : IsPrimitive v) : Slope M

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.mk_eq_mk
decls.statement:
theorem mk_eq_mk {v w : M} (hv : IsPrimitive v) (hw : IsPrimitive w)
    (h : v = w ∨ v = -w) : mk v hv = mk w hw

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.mk_eq_mk_iff
decls.doc: Two primitive representatives define the same slope exactly when they agree up to sign.
decls.statement:
theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {v w : M} (hv : IsPrimitive v) (hw : IsPrimitive w) :
    mk v hv = mk w hw ↔ v = w ∨ v = -w

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.induction_on
decls.statement:
theorem induction_on {C : Slope M → Prop} (s : Slope M)
    (h : ∀ (v : M) (hv : IsPrimitive v), C (mk v hv)) : C s

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.congr
decls.doc:
A `ℤ`-linear equivalence `M ≃ₗ[ℤ] N` transports slopes bijectively; a framing's coordinate
isomorphism uses this to carry a slope to the standard lattice.
decls.statement: def congr (φ : M ≃ₗ[ℤ] N) : Slope M ≃ Slope N

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.congr_mk
decls.statement:
theorem congr_mk (φ : M ≃ₗ[ℤ] N) (v : M) (h : IsPrimitive v) :
    congr φ (mk v h) = mk (φ v) ((isPrimitive_congr φ).mpr h)

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.congr_symm
decls.doc: Transporting slopes along `φ` and along `φ.symm` are inverse to one another.
decls.statement: theorem congr_symm (φ : M ≃ₗ[ℤ] N) : (congr φ).symm = congr φ.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_prod_iff
decls.doc: Over `ℤ × ℤ`, a class is primitive exactly when its two coordinates are coprime.
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_prod_iff {v : ℤ × ℤ} : IsPrimitive v ↔ IsCoprime v.1 v.2

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_prod_one_zero
decls.doc: The first standard basis vector of `ℤ × ℤ` is primitive.
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_prod_one_zero : IsPrimitive ((1, 0) : ℤ × ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_prod_zero_one
decls.doc: The second standard basis vector of `ℤ × ℤ` is primitive.
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_prod_zero_one : IsPrimitive ((0, 1) : ℤ × ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_num_den
decls.doc: The reduced form `(r.num, r.den)` of a rational is a primitive class.
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_num_den (r : ℚ) : IsPrimitive ((r.num, (r.den : ℤ)) : ℤ × ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPrimitive_prod_fst_eq_one_or_neg_one_of_snd_eq_zero
decls.doc: A primitive class of `ℤ × ℤ` with vanishing second coordinate has first coordinate `±1`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPrimitive_prod_fst_eq_one_or_neg_one_of_snd_eq_zero {v : ℤ × ℤ} (h : IsPrimitive v)
    (hq : v.2 = 0) : v.1 = 1 ∨ v.1 = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeValue
decls.doc:
The value `p / q ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}` of a class `v = (p, q)`, taken to be `∞` when `q = 0`. This is the
ratio of the meridian- and longitude-coordinates in a framing.
decls.statement: def slopeValue (v : ℤ × ℤ) : OnePoint ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeValue_of_snd_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem slopeValue_of_snd_eq_zero {v : ℤ × ℤ} (hq : v.2 = 0) : slopeValue v = ∞

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeValue_of_snd_ne_zero
decls.statement:
theorem slopeValue_of_snd_ne_zero {v : ℤ × ℤ} (hq : v.2 ≠ 0) :
    slopeValue v = ((v.1 : ℚ) / (v.2 : ℚ) : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeValue_neg
decls.doc: The value of a class is unchanged by the sign action `v ↦ -v`.
decls.statement: theorem slopeValue_neg (v : ℤ × ℤ) : slopeValue (-v) = slopeValue v

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.value
decls.doc: The `ℚ ∪ {∞}` value of a standard-lattice slope, the ratio of its coordinates.
decls.statement: def Slope.value : Slope (ℤ × ℤ) → OnePoint ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.Slope.value_mk
decls.statement:
theorem Slope.value_mk (v : ℤ × ℤ) (h : IsPrimitive v) :
    Slope.value (Slope.mk v h) = slopeValue v

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeOfValue
decls.doc:
The primitive class attached to a value in `ℚ ∪ {∞}`: the class `(1, 0)` for `∞`, and the
reduced fraction `(r.num, r.den)` for a rational `r`.
decls.statement: def slopeOfValue : OnePoint ℚ → Slope (ℤ × ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeOfValue_infty
decls.statement: theorem slopeOfValue_infty : slopeOfValue ∞ = Slope.mk (1, 0) isPrimitive_prod_one_zero

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeOfValue_coe
decls.statement:
theorem slopeOfValue_coe (r : ℚ) :
    slopeOfValue (r : OnePoint ℚ) = Slope.mk (r.num, (r.den : ℤ)) (isPrimitive_num_den r)

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeOfValue_value
decls.doc:
Reading off the value of a standard-lattice slope and rebuilding a slope from it recovers the
original slope.
decls.statement: theorem slopeOfValue_value (s : Slope (ℤ × ℤ)) : slopeOfValue (Slope.value s) = s

decls.name: TauCeti.value_slopeOfValue
decls.doc: The standard-lattice slope built from a value in `ℚ ∪ {∞}` has that value again.
decls.statement: theorem value_slopeOfValue (x : OnePoint ℚ) : Slope.value (slopeOfValue x) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeEquivStd
decls.doc:
**The standard slope parametrisation.** For the standard lattice `ℤ × ℤ`, primitive homology
classes modulo sign biject with `ℚ ∪ {∞}`: a reduced fraction `p / q` corresponds to the primitive
class `(p, q)`, with `∞` the class `(1, 0)`. A framing produces the corresponding bijection on
any boundary torus through its coordinate isomorphism (`TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv`).
decls.title: The standard slope parametrisation
decls.statement: def slopeEquivStd : Slope (ℤ × ℤ) ≃ OnePoint ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeEquivStd_apply
decls.statement: theorem slopeEquivStd_apply (s : Slope (ℤ × ℤ)) : slopeEquivStd s = Slope.value s

decls.name: TauCeti.slopeEquivStd_symm_apply
decls.statement: theorem slopeEquivStd_symm_apply (x : OnePoint ℚ) : slopeEquivStd.symm x = slopeOfValue x

decls.name: TauCeti.BoundaryTorus
decls.doc:
A **boundary torus** is a topological space that is homeomorphic to the standard two-torus; no
particular homeomorphism is chosen. Its first homology, rather than an unrelated abstract lattice,
is the carrier on which slopes are defined.
decls.statement: structure BoundaryTorus

decls.name: TauCeti.BoundaryTorus.firstHomology
decls.doc: The first singular homology of a boundary torus with integer coefficients.
decls.statement: abbrev firstHomology (T : BoundaryTorus) : Type

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus
decls.doc:
A **framed boundary torus**: a boundary torus together with an ordered
meridian-longitude basis `(μ, λ) = (basis 0, basis 1)` of its actual singular homology group.
The framing is exactly this ordered basis; it is what identifies `H₁(T; ℤ)` with `ℤ × ℤ` and so
what the `ℚ ∪ {∞}` parametrisation depends on.
decls.statement: structure FramedBoundaryTorus

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.H
decls.doc: The first singular homology group of the underlying boundary torus.
decls.statement: abbrev H (T : FramedBoundaryTorus)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord
decls.doc:
The coordinate isomorphism `H₁(T; ℤ) ≃ ℤ × ℤ` induced by the ordered basis `(μ, λ)`, sending a
class to its `(μ, λ)`-coordinates. This is the data that makes the parametrisation
basis-dependent.
decls.statement: def coord : T.H ≃ₗ[ℤ] ℤ × ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_basis_zero
decls.statement: theorem coord_basis_zero : T.coord (T.basis 0) = (1, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_basis_one
decls.statement: theorem coord_basis_one : T.coord (T.basis 1) = (0, 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse coordinate isomorphism reads a pair of coordinates as the corresponding
combination `p · μ + q · λ` of the framing basis.
decls.statement: theorem coord_symm_apply (v : ℤ × ℤ) : T.coord.symm v = v.1 • T.basis 0 + v.2 • T.basis 1

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.isPrimitive_basis_zero
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_basis_zero : IsPrimitive (T.basis 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.isPrimitive_basis_one
decls.statement: theorem isPrimitive_basis_one : IsPrimitive (T.basis 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.meridian
decls.doc: The meridian slope `μ = basis 0` of the framing.
decls.statement: def meridian : Slope T.H

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.longitude
decls.doc: The longitude slope `λ = basis 1` of the framing.
decls.statement: def longitude : Slope T.H

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value
decls.doc:
The framing-dependent value `p / q ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}` of a slope: the ratio of its `(μ, λ)`-coordinates.
Different framings give different values, which is why this is an operation of the framing rather
than of the basis-free `Slope`.
decls.statement: def value (s : Slope T.H) : OnePoint ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv
decls.doc:
**The framed slope parametrisation.** A framing makes primitive homology classes modulo sign
biject with `ℚ ∪ {∞}`, a reduced fraction `p / q` corresponding to the class with
`(μ, λ)`-coordinates `(p, q)` and `∞` to the meridian.
decls.title: The framed slope parametrisation
decls.statement: def slopeEquiv : Slope T.H ≃ OnePoint ℚ

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv_apply
decls.statement: theorem slopeEquiv_apply (s : Slope T.H) : T.slopeEquiv s = T.value s

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value_mk
decls.doc: The value of the slope of a primitive class is the ratio of its `(μ, λ)`-coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem value_mk (v : T.H) (hv : IsPrimitive v) :
    T.value (Slope.mk v hv) = slopeValue (T.coord v)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
**The framed parametrisation in the inverse direction.** The slope with value `x ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}` is
the one whose `(μ, λ)`-coordinates are the standard reduced pair `slopeOfValue x`; for a rational
`p / q` in lowest terms that is the class `p · μ + q · λ`, by
`TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_symm_apply`.
decls.title: The framed parametrisation in the inverse direction
decls.statement:
theorem slopeEquiv_symm_apply (x : OnePoint ℚ) :
    T.slopeEquiv.symm x = Slope.congr T.coord.symm (slopeOfValue x)

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value_meridian
decls.doc: The framed meridian has slope value `∞`.
decls.statement: theorem value_meridian : T.value T.meridian = ∞

decls.name: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value_longitude
decls.doc: The framed longitude has slope value `0`.
decls.statement: theorem value_longitude : T.value T.longitude = (0 : ℚ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv
decls.doc:
The total-transform identification of the blown-up plumbing lattice.

A pair `(x, s)` consisting of a lattice point `x` of the original plumbing and a multiple `s` of
the exceptional class is sent to the lattice point of the blow-up whose coordinate at the new
vertex `none` is `x v + s` and whose coordinate at an old vertex `some w` is `x w`. On basis
vectors this is `e_v ↦ e_v + e_none` (the total transform, or pullback, of the blown-up sphere),
`e_w ↦ e_w` for `w ≠ v`, and `(0, 1) ↦ e_none`; see `blowUpVertexEquiv_zero_one`. The proper
transform of the blown-up sphere is instead the basis vector `Pi.single (some v) 1`, the image of
`(e_v, -1)`; unlike the total transform it meets the exceptional class once.

The map depends only on the blown-up vertex, not on the framings or the edges.
decls.statement: def blowUpVertexEquiv (v : V) : ((V → ℤ) × ℤ) ≃ₗ[ℤ] (Option V → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv_apply_none
decls.doc: The coordinate of a lifted lattice point at the new vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexEquiv_apply_none (v : V) (x : V → ℤ) (s : ℤ) :
    blowUpVertexEquiv v (x, s) none = x v + s

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv_apply_some
decls.doc: The coordinate of a lifted lattice point at an old vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexEquiv_apply_some (v : V) (x : V → ℤ) (s : ℤ) (w : V) :
    blowUpVertexEquiv v (x, s) (some w) = x w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse identification reads off the old coordinates and the exceptional multiplicity.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexEquiv_symm_apply (v : V) (y : Option V → ℤ) :
    (blowUpVertexEquiv v).symm y = (fun w => y (some w), y none - y (some v))

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv_zero_one
decls.doc: The pair `(0, 1)` is the exceptional class, the basis vector at the new vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexEquiv_zero_one [DecidableEq V] (v : V) :
    blowUpVertexEquiv v (0, 1) = Pi.single (none : Option V) (1 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.BlowUpVertexAdj
decls.doc:
The adjacency relation of the blow-up of a plumbing graph at a vertex: the new vertex `none`
is joined exactly to `some v`, and the old vertices keep their adjacencies.

This is internal to the construction of `blowUpVertex`; consumers use the adjacency lemmas
`blowUpVertex_adj_none_some`, `blowUpVertex_adj_some_none` and `blowUpVertex_adj_some_some`.
decls.statement: def BlowUpVertexAdj (P : PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) : Option V → Option V → Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.decidableBlowUpVertexAdj
decls.statement:
instance decidableBlowUpVertexAdj [DecidableEq V] (P : PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) :
    DecidableRel (P.BlowUpVertexAdj v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexAdj_symm
decls.doc: The blow-up adjacency relation is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexAdj_symm (P : PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) :
    Std.Symm (P.BlowUpVertexAdj v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexAdj_irrefl
decls.doc: The blow-up adjacency relation is irreflexive.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertexAdj_irrefl (P : PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) :
    Std.Irrefl (P.BlowUpVertexAdj v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex
decls.doc:
The blow-up of a plumbing graph at a vertex `v`: adjoin a new vertex `none` with framing `-1`,
join it to `some v`, and drop the framing of `some v` by one.

This is the plumbing move corresponding to blowing up a point on the sphere `v`; the plumbed
three-manifold at the boundary is unchanged, while the plumbed four-manifold gains a `-1`-sphere.
decls.statement: def blowUpVertex [DecidableEq V] (P : PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) : PlumbingGraph (Option V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_adj_none_some
decls.doc: The new vertex is joined exactly to the blown-up vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_adj_none_some (w : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).toSimpleGraph.Adj none (some w) ↔ w = v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_adj_some_none
decls.doc: The new vertex is joined exactly to the blown-up vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_adj_some_none (w : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).toSimpleGraph.Adj (some w) none ↔ w = v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_adj_some_some
decls.doc: The blow-up keeps all adjacencies between old vertices.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_adj_some_some (w w' : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).toSimpleGraph.Adj (some w) (some w') ↔ P.toSimpleGraph.Adj w w'

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_weight_none
decls.doc: The new vertex is `-1`-framed.
decls.statement: theorem blowUpVertex_weight_none : (P.blowUpVertex v).weight none = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_weight_some
decls.doc: The framings of the old vertices, with the blown-up one dropped by a unit.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_weight_some (w : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).weight (some w) = if w = v then P.weight w - 1 else P.weight w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_weight_some_self
decls.doc: Blowing up drops the framing of the blown-up vertex by a unit.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_weight_some_self :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).weight (some v) = P.weight v - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_weight_some_of_ne
decls.doc: Blowing up leaves the framings of the other vertices alone.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_weight_some_of_ne {w : V} (h : w ≠ v) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).weight (some w) = P.weight w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_neighborSet_none
decls.doc: The new vertex has exactly one neighbour, the blown-up vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_neighborSet_none :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).toSimpleGraph.neighborSet none = {some v}

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_degree_none
decls.doc:
The new vertex has degree one. Together with its framing `-1` this is exactly the local
configuration that Neumann's blow-down move removes.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_degree_none [Fintype V] :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).toSimpleGraph.degree none = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_none_none
decls.doc:
The exceptional sphere has self-intersection `-1`. This is not a `simp` lemma: the simp set
already rewrites the left-hand side through `intersectionMatrix_diag` and
`blowUpVertex_weight_none`.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_none_none :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix none none = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_none_some
decls.doc:
The exceptional sphere meets the proper transform `Pi.single (some v) 1` once and the other
spheres not at all.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_none_some (w : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix none (some w) = if w = v then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_some_none
decls.doc:
The exceptional sphere meets the proper transform `Pi.single (some v) 1` once and the other
spheres not at all.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_some_none (w : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix (some w) none = if w = v then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_some_some
decls.doc:
Between old vertices the intersection matrix changes only in the diagonal entry of the
blown-up vertex, which drops by a unit.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_intersectionMatrix_some_some (w w' : V) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix (some w) (some w') =
      P.intersectionMatrix w w' -
        (if w = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0) * (if w' = v then (1 : ℤ) else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_mulVec_apply_none
decls.doc:
The `none`-coordinate of the image of a lifted lattice point under the blown-up intersection
matrix: the exceptional class is orthogonal to the total transforms, so only the exceptional
multiplicity survives.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_mulVec_apply_none (y : V → ℤ) (t : ℤ) :
    ((P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix *ᵥ blowUpVertexEquiv v (y, t)) none = -t

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertex_mulVec_apply_some
decls.doc:
The `some`-coordinates of the image of a lifted lattice point under the blown-up intersection
matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem blowUpVertex_mulVec_apply_some (y : V → ℤ) (t : ℤ) (w : V) :
    ((P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionMatrix *ᵥ blowUpVertexEquiv v (y, t)) (some w) =
      (P.intersectionMatrix *ᵥ y) w + (if w = v then t else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_blowUpVertexEquiv
decls.doc:
**The blow-up splits the intersection form.** Under the total-transform identification
`blowUpVertexEquiv`, the intersection form of the blow-up is the orthogonal direct sum of the
intersection form of `P` with the rank-one form `⟨-1⟩` spanned by the exceptional class.
decls.title: The blow-up splits the intersection form
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_blowUpVertexEquiv (x y : V → ℤ) (s t : ℤ) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionForm (blowUpVertexEquiv v (x, s))
        (blowUpVertexEquiv v (y, t)) =
      P.intersectionForm x y - s * t

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_single_none_self
decls.doc: The exceptional class has self-intersection `-1`.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_single_none_self :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionForm (Pi.single (none : Option V) (1 : ℤ))
        (Pi.single (none : Option V) (1 : ℤ)) = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_blowUpVertexEquiv_single_none
decls.doc:
The exceptional class is orthogonal to every total transform, so the splitting of
`intersectionForm_blowUpVertexEquiv` really is orthogonal.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_blowUpVertexEquiv_single_none (x : V → ℤ) :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).intersectionForm (blowUpVertexEquiv v (x, 0))
        (Pi.single (none : Option V) (1 : ℤ)) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isNegativeDefinite_blowUpVertex_iff
decls.doc:
**Blowing up at a vertex preserves and reflects negative-definiteness.** The blown-up
intersection form is the old one plus a `⟨-1⟩` summand, so it is negative definite exactly when
the old one is. Since negative-definiteness is the standing hypothesis of lattice homology, the
blow-up move stays inside the class of plumbings the theory applies to.

Exposed to `grind` as a rewrite, like the other `IsNegativeDefinite` characterizations, so that
`grind` reduces negative-definiteness of a blow-up to negative-definiteness of `P`.
decls.title: Blowing up at a vertex preserves and reflects negative-definiteness
decls.statement:
theorem isNegativeDefinite_blowUpVertex_iff [Finite V] :
    (P.blowUpVertex v).IsNegativeDefinite ↔ P.IsNegativeDefinite

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector
decls.doc:
A covector of the plumbing lattice is characteristic when its value on every basis sphere is
congruent modulo two to that sphere's self-intersection. For the plumbing basis this is the
usual condition `k(v) ≡ v · v (mod 2)`, since `v · v = P.weight v`.
decls.statement: def IsCharacteristicVector (k : V → ℤ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicVectors
decls.doc: The subtype of characteristic covectors of the plumbing lattice.
decls.statement: abbrev characteristicVectors

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isCharacteristicVector_iff
decls.doc:
Characteristic covectors are exactly the covectors satisfying the vertex-wise parity
condition. This is a `_def`-style restatement: it is not a `@[simp]` lemma, so that the
per-instance characteristic lemmas (such as `isCharacteristicVector_canonicalCharacteristic`)
keep their `IsCharacteristicVector` head for `simp` to match; it is exposed to `grind` for
unfolding the predicate.
decls.statement:
theorem isCharacteristicVector_iff (k : V → ℤ) :
    P.IsCharacteristicVector k ↔ ∀ v : V, k v ≡ P.weight v [ZMOD 2]

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.canonicalCharacteristic
decls.doc:
The canonical characteristic covector, in the plumbing convention
`K(E_v) + E_v · E_v = -2`. Since `E_v · E_v = P.weight v`, its coordinate at `v` is
`-P.weight v - 2`. The body is not part of the interface: use `canonicalCharacteristic_apply`
for its coordinates and the characteristic/adjunction lemmas below.
decls.statement: def canonicalCharacteristic : V → ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.canonicalCharacteristic_apply
decls.doc: The canonical characteristic covector has coordinates `-P.weight v - 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem canonicalCharacteristic_apply (v : V) :
    P.canonicalCharacteristic v = -P.weight v - 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isCharacteristicVector_canonicalCharacteristic
decls.doc: The canonical covector is characteristic.
decls.statement:
theorem isCharacteristicVector_canonicalCharacteristic :
    P.IsCharacteristicVector P.canonicalCharacteristic

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.zmod_two_sq
decls.statement: theorem zmod_two_sq (a : ZMod 2) : a ^ 2 = a

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.adjacency_sum_cast_zmod_two_eq_zero
decls.statement:
theorem adjacency_sum_cast_zmod_two_eq_zero (x : V → ℤ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, ((if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then x i * x j else 0 : ℤ) : ZMod 2)) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isCharacteristicVector_iff_intersection_single
decls.doc: Characteristicness can be read from the self-pairing of the plumbing basis vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem isCharacteristicVector_iff_intersection_single (k : V → ℤ) :
    P.IsCharacteristicVector k ↔
      ∀ v : V, k v ≡ P.intersectionForm (Pi.single v 1) (Pi.single v 1) [ZMOD 2]

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isCharacteristicVector_iff_forall_modEq_intersectionForm
decls.doc:
A covector is characteristic exactly when its evaluation on every lattice vector is congruent
modulo two to that vector's self-pairing under the plumbing intersection form.
decls.statement:
theorem isCharacteristicVector_iff_forall_modEq_intersectionForm (k : V → ℤ) :
    P.IsCharacteristicVector k ↔
      ∀ x : V → ℤ, (∑ v, k v * x v) ≡ P.intersectionForm x x [ZMOD 2]

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.canonicalCharacteristic_apply_add_intersection_single
decls.doc:
The canonical characteristic covector satisfies the adjunction coordinate equation
`K(E_v) + E_v · E_v = -2`.
decls.statement:
theorem canonicalCharacteristic_apply_add_intersection_single (v : V) :
    P.canonicalCharacteristic v +
      P.intersectionForm (Pi.single v 1) (Pi.single v 1) = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.add_of_forall_even
decls.doc: Adding an even-valued covector preserves characteristicness.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.add_two_mul
decls.doc: Adding twice an integral covector preserves characteristicness.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCharacteristicVector.add_two_mul {k l : V → ℤ}
    (hk : P.IsCharacteristicVector k) : P.IsCharacteristicVector fun v => k v + 2 * l v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.neg
decls.doc: Negating a characteristic covector preserves characteristicness.
decls.statement:
theorem IsCharacteristicVector.neg {k : V → ℤ}
    (hk : P.IsCharacteristicVector k) : P.IsCharacteristicVector fun v => -k v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.conjugate
decls.doc:
Spin^c conjugation on characteristic covectors: negate the covector. Characteristicness is
preserved because `-1 ≡ 1 [ZMOD 2]` (see `IsCharacteristicVector.neg`), so this is a well-defined
involution of `characteristicVectors`. On the level of spin^c structures it is the conjugation
involution.
decls.statement: def conjugate (k : P.characteristicVectors) : P.characteristicVectors

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.conjugate_val_aux
decls.doc: The conjugate covector is the pointwise negation of the original.
decls.statement: theorem conjugate_val_aux (k : P.characteristicVectors) : (P.conjugate k).val = -k.val

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.conjugate_val
decls.doc: The conjugate covector is the pointwise negation of the original.
decls.statement: theorem conjugate_val (k : P.characteristicVectors) : (P.conjugate k).val = -k.val

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.conjugate_conjugate
decls.doc: Spin^c conjugation is an involution.
decls.statement:
theorem conjugate_conjugate (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.conjugate (P.conjugate k) = k

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.even_sub
decls.doc: The pointwise difference of two characteristic covectors is even.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.sub_modEq_zero
decls.doc: The pointwise difference of two characteristic covectors is congruent to zero modulo two.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isCharacteristicVector_canonical_add_two_mul
decls.doc:
A covector obtained from the canonical characteristic covector by adding twice another
covector is characteristic.
decls.statement:
theorem isCharacteristicVector_canonical_add_two_mul (l : V → ℤ) :
    P.IsCharacteristicVector fun v => P.canonicalCharacteristic v + 2 * l v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsCharacteristicVector.even_sub_canonical
decls.doc:
A characteristic covector differs from the canonical characteristic covector by an
even-valued covector.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_neg_neg
decls.doc:
Negating both the covector and the lattice point fixes the weight numerator: each linear term
`k v * x v` is unchanged and the quadratic term `x · x` is even in `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_neg_neg (k x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator (-k) (-x) = P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_neg_left
decls.doc:
Negating only the covector reflects the weight numerator through `2 (x · x)`: the quadratic
term is untouched while the linear term changes sign.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_neg_left (k x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator (-k) x =
      2 * P.intersectionForm x x - P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_conjugate_neg
decls.doc:
**Conjugation symmetry of the lattice weight.** Conjugating the covector and negating the
lattice point leaves the characteristic weight unchanged: `χ_{-k}(-x) = χ_k(x)`. This is the
identity behind the conjugation involution of lattice homology.
decls.title: Conjugation symmetry of the lattice weight
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_conjugate_neg (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight (P.conjugate k) (-x) = P.characteristicWeight k x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_conjugate_add
decls.doc:
The conjugate and original weights at a fixed lattice point sum to `-(x · x)`: a linear
relation expressing the conjugate weight through the intersection form.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_conjugate_add (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight (P.conjugate k) x + P.characteristicWeight k x =
      -P.intersectionForm x x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_conjugate_canonical_single
decls.doc:
The conjugate of the canonical characteristic covector has weight `-P.weight v - 1` on the
plumbing basis sphere at `v`.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_conjugate_canonical_single (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeight
      (P.conjugate ⟨P.canonicalCharacteristic, P.isCharacteristicVector_canonicalCharacteristic⟩)
      (Pi.single v 1) = -P.weight v - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_injective
decls.doc:
Distinct subsets of basis directions determine distinct vertices of a plumbing-lattice cube.

At coordinate `v`, the vertex remembers whether `v` was selected by adding `1` precisely in the
selected directions, so equality of vertices recovers membership in the subset.
decls.statement: theorem cubeVertex_injective (x : V → ℤ) : Function.Injective (cubeVertex x)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertexSubsetEquiv
decls.doc:
The equivalence between subsets of the direction set and vertices of the corresponding
plumbing-lattice cube. This is the precise "one vertex for each subset of directions" statement
behind the cardinality formula.
decls.statement:
def cubeVertexSubsetEquiv (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    {T : Finset V // T ⊆ S} ≃ {y : V → ℤ // y ∈ cubeVertices x S}

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply_aux
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply_aux
    (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (T : {T : Finset V // T ⊆ S}) :
    (cubeVertexSubsetEquiv x S T).1 = cubeVertex x T.1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The subset-to-vertex equivalence sends a subset of directions to its cube vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (T : {T : Finset V // T ⊆ S}) :
    (cubeVertexSubsetEquiv x S T).1 = cubeVertex x T.1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of the subset-to-vertex equivalence returns a subset whose vertex is the
specified cube vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertexSubsetEquiv_apply_symm_apply (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V)
    (y : {y : V → ℤ // y ∈ cubeVertices x S}) :
    cubeVertex x ((cubeVertexSubsetEquiv x S).symm y).1 = y.1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_eq_image_powerset
decls.doc:
The vertex set of the cube with direction set `S` is exactly the image of the powerset of
`S` under the subset-to-vertex map.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertices_eq_image_powerset (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    cubeVertices x S = S.powerset.image (cubeVertex x)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.card_cubeVertices
decls.doc: A plumbing-lattice cube with direction set `S` has one vertex for each subset of `S`.
decls.statement:
theorem card_cubeVertices (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    (cubeVertices x S).card = 2 ^ S.card

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_upperFace_subset
decls.doc: The upper face in a direction has its vertices among the vertices of the ambient cube.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertices_upperFace_subset {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    cubeVertices (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v) ⊆ cubeVertices x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicUpperFaceWeight_le
decls.doc: The upper face's characteristic cube weight is bounded by the ambient cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceWeight_le {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v) ≤
      P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicLowerFaceExponent
decls.doc: The nonnegative `U`-exponent contributed by the lower face in a cube direction.
decls.statement:
def characteristicLowerFaceExponent
    (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast
decls.doc:
The lower-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the ambient cube weight
and the lower face weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast
    {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} :
    (P.characteristicLowerFaceExponent k x S v : ℤ) =
      P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S - P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (S.erase v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The lower-face exponent is zero exactly when the lower face has the same weight as the
ambient cube.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
    {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} :
    P.characteristicLowerFaceExponent k x S v = 0 ↔
      P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S = P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (S.erase v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicUpperFaceExponent
decls.doc: The nonnegative `U`-exponent contributed by the upper face in a direction.
decls.statement:
def characteristicUpperFaceExponent
    (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) {v : V} (_hv : v ∈ S) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast
decls.doc:
The upper-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the ambient cube weight
and the upper face weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast
    {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    (P.characteristicUpperFaceExponent k x S hv : ℤ) =
      P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S -
        P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The upper-face exponent is zero exactly when the upper face has the same weight as the
ambient cube.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
    {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    P.characteristicUpperFaceExponent k x S hv = 0 ↔
      P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S =
        P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast_lowerFace
decls.doc:
The lower-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight
and the lower face weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast_lowerFace
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v : ℤ) =
      characteristicWeight P k C - characteristicWeight P k (C.lowerFace v hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
decls.doc: The lower-lower codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent along either path.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace v hv) w =
      characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C w +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace w hw) v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
decls.doc: The upper-upper codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent along either path.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := v) hv +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace v hv)
          (v := w)
          (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := w) hw +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace w hw)
          (v := v)
          (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
decls.doc:
The lower-then-upper mixed codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent as the
upper-then-lower path to the same corner.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace v hv)
          (v := w)
          (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := w) hw +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace w hw) v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
decls.doc:
The upper-then-lower mixed codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent as the
lower-then-upper path to the same corner.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := v) hv +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace v hv) w =
      characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C w +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace w hw)
          (v := v)
          (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube
decls.doc:
A plumbing-lattice cube generator: a lattice base point together with a finite set of basis
directions. In Némethi's lattice homology this is the cubical generator usually denoted by a pair
`(x, S)`.
decls.statement: structure PlumbingCube (V : Type*)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.ext
decls.doc: Two plumbing cubes are equal when their base points and direction sets agree.
decls.statement:
theorem ext {C D : PlumbingCube V} (hbase : C.base = D.base)
    (hdirections : C.directions = D.directions) : C = D

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.dimension
decls.doc: The cubical dimension of a plumbing cube, namely the number of basis directions.
decls.statement: abbrev dimension (C : PlumbingCube V) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.eraseDirection
decls.doc:
The raw lower cube obtained by keeping the base point and erasing a direction from the direction
set. If the direction is absent, this is the original cube.
decls.statement: irreducible_def eraseDirection (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.eraseDirection_def
decls.statement: irreducible_def eraseDirection (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace
decls.doc:
The lower codimension-one face in a present direction `v`: keep the base point and remove `v`
from the direction set.
decls.statement:
irreducible_def lowerFace (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V)
    (_hv : v ∈ C.directions) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_def
decls.statement:
irreducible_def lowerFace (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V)
    (_hv : v ∈ C.directions) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace
decls.doc:
The upper codimension-one face in a present direction `v`: shift the base point by `E_v` and
remove `v` from the direction set.
decls.statement:
irreducible_def upperFace (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V)
    (_hv : v ∈ C.directions) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_def
decls.statement:
irreducible_def upperFace (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V)
    (_hv : v ∈ C.directions) : PlumbingCube V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.dimension_mk
decls.statement:
theorem dimension_mk (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    dimension ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) = S.card

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.eraseDirection_mk
decls.statement:
theorem eraseDirection_mk (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) :
    eraseDirection ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) v =
      ({ base := x, directions := S.erase v } : PlumbingCube V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_mk
decls.statement:
theorem lowerFace_mk (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ S) :
    lowerFace ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) v hv =
      ({ base := x, directions := S.erase v } : PlumbingCube V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_mk
decls.statement:
theorem upperFace_mk (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ S) :
    upperFace ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) v hv =
      ({ base := x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ), directions := S.erase v } : PlumbingCube V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.eraseDirection_base
decls.statement:
theorem eraseDirection_base (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    (C.eraseDirection v).base = C.base

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.eraseDirection_directions
decls.statement:
theorem eraseDirection_directions (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    (C.eraseDirection v).directions = C.directions.erase v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_base
decls.statement:
theorem lowerFace_base (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (C.lowerFace v hv).base = C.base

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_directions
decls.statement:
theorem lowerFace_directions (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (C.lowerFace v hv).directions = C.directions.erase v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_base
decls.statement:
theorem upperFace_base (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (C.upperFace v hv).base = C.base + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_directions
decls.statement:
theorem upperFace_directions (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (C.upperFace v hv).directions = C.directions.erase v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.vertices
decls.doc: The vertices of a bundled plumbing cube.
decls.statement: irreducible_def vertices (C : PlumbingCube V) : Finset (V → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.vertices_def
decls.statement: irreducible_def vertices (C : PlumbingCube V) : Finset (V → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.vertices_mk
decls.statement:
theorem vertices_mk (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    vertices ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) =
      PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.mem_vertices
decls.doc: Membership in the vertices of a bundled cube, expressed by a direction subset.
decls.statement:

decls.doc: The base point is a vertex of every bundled cube.
decls.statement:

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.vertices_upperFace_subset

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.vertices_eq_union_faces

The vertices of a bundled cube split as the union of the vertices of its lower and upper faces
in any present direction.
decls.statement:
theorem vertices_eq_union_faces (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    C.vertices = (C.lowerFace v hv).vertices ∪ (C.upperFace v hv).vertices

irreducible_def characteristicWeight [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_mk

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent
decls.doc:
The nonnegative `U`-exponent contributed by the raw lower cube obtained by erasing a direction.
When the direction is present, this is the exponent of the lower face.
decls.statement:
irreducible_def characteristicLowerFaceExponent [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_def
decls.statement:
irreducible_def characteristicLowerFaceExponent [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent
decls.doc: The nonnegative `U`-exponent contributed by the upper face of a bundled cube.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_def
TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_mk
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_mk [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) v =

decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_mk [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)

    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) hv =
      P.characteristicUpperFaceExponent k x S hv

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast
decls.doc:
The lower exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight and the
weight after erasing the direction.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    (characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v : ℤ) =
      characteristicWeight P k C - characteristicWeight P k (C.eraseDirection v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast
decls.doc:
The upper-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight
and the upper face weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C hv : ℤ) =
      characteristicWeight P k C - characteristicWeight P k (C.upperFace v hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The lower exponent is zero exactly when erasing the direction leaves the bundled weight
unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v = 0 ↔
      characteristicWeight P k C = characteristicWeight P k (C.eraseDirection v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The upper-face exponent is zero exactly when the upper face has the same bundled weight as the
ambient cube.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C hv = 0 ↔
      characteristicWeight P k C = characteristicWeight P k (C.upperFace v hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.min_characteristicFaceExponent_eq_zero
decls.doc: In any bundled cube direction, at least one face exponent is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem min_characteristicFaceExponent_eq_zero [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    min (characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v)
      (characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C hv) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_eraseDirection_le
decls.doc:
Erasing a direction gives a cube whose characteristic weight is bounded by the ambient cube
weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_eraseDirection_le [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    characteristicWeight P k (C.eraseDirection v) ≤ characteristicWeight P k C

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_lowerFace_le
decls.doc: The lower face's characteristic weight is bounded by the ambient cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_lowerFace_le [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicWeight P k (C.lowerFace v hv) ≤ characteristicWeight P k C

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_upperFace_le
decls.doc: The upper face's characteristic weight is bounded by the ambient cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_upperFace_le [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicWeight P k (C.upperFace v hv) ≤ characteristicWeight P k C

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_eq_max_faces
decls.doc:
In any present direction, the characteristic weight of a cube is the maximum of the weights
of its lower and upper faces.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_eq_max_faces [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicWeight P k C =
      max (characteristicWeight P k (C.lowerFace v hv))
        (characteristicWeight P k (C.upperFace v hv))

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_lowerFace_comm
decls.doc:
The two lower faces in distinct directions `v` and `w` agree: both are the cube based at
`C.base` with directions `(C.directions.erase v).erase w`.
decls.statement:
theorem lowerFace_lowerFace_comm (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    (C.lowerFace v hv).lowerFace w
        (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      (C.lowerFace w hw).lowerFace v
        (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_upperFace_comm
decls.doc:
The two upper faces in distinct directions `v` and `w` agree: both are the cube based at
`C.base + E_v + E_w` with directions `(C.directions.erase v).erase w`, since the two basis shifts
commute.
decls.statement:
theorem upperFace_upperFace_comm (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    (C.upperFace v hv).upperFace w
        (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      (C.upperFace w hw).upperFace v
        (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.lowerFace_upperFace_comm
decls.doc:
Taking the lower face in direction `v` then the upper face in direction `w` agrees with taking
the upper face in direction `w` then the lower face in direction `v`: both are the mixed corner
based at `C.base + E_w`.
decls.statement:
theorem lowerFace_upperFace_comm (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    (C.lowerFace v hv).upperFace w
        (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      (C.upperFace w hw).lowerFace v
        (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.upperFace_lowerFace_comm
decls.doc:
Taking the upper face in direction `v` then the lower face in direction `w` agrees with taking
the lower face in direction `w` then the upper face in direction `v`: both are the mixed corner
based at `C.base + E_v`.
decls.statement:
theorem upperFace_lowerFace_comm (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.sum_mul_sum_single
decls.doc:
The characteristic covector paired against a finite sum of basis spheres selects the covector
coordinates in the chosen directions.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_mul_sum_single (k : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    (∑ w, k w * (∑ v ∈ S, Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) w) = ∑ w ∈ S, k w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_cubeVertex
decls.doc:
**The cube-vertex weight numerator in coordinates.** The weight numerator at the vertex
`cubeVertex x S = x + ∑ v ∈ S, E_v` of a plumbing cube is the base numerator, plus the covector
coordinates in the chosen directions, plus the intersection double sum of those directions, plus
twice the pairings of the base point against them. As the numerator carries no division, this is
the formula a concrete cube-weight computation evaluates.
decls.title: The cube-vertex weight numerator in coordinates
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_cubeVertex (k x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator k (cubeVertex x S) =
      P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x + (∑ v ∈ S, k v) +
        (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, P.intersectionMatrix v w) +
        2 * ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ i, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_cubeVertex
decls.doc:
**The cube-vertex weight through the base point.** The weight at the vertex
`cubeVertex x S = x + ∑ v ∈ S, E_v` splits, by the polarization identity, into the base weight, the
weight of the pure sphere sum `∑ v ∈ S, E_v`, and the linear pairings of the base point against the
moving spheres.
decls.title: The cube-vertex weight through the base point
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_cubeVertex (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (cubeVertex x S) =
      P.characteristicWeight k x + P.characteristicWeight k (∑ v ∈ S, Pi.single v 1) -
        ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ i, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex
decls.doc:
The lattice point obtained from a base point `x` by adding the plumbing basis vectors in
`T`. This is the vertex of a lattice cube indexed by the subset `T` of its directions.
decls.statement: def cubeVertex (x : V → ℤ) (T : Finset V) : V → ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_def
decls.doc:
A plumbing cube vertex is the base point shifted by the basis spheres in the chosen
directions. This is definitionally `cubeVertex`, packaged for rewriting.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_def (x : V → ℤ) (T : Finset V) :
    cubeVertex x T = x + ∑ v ∈ T, Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_empty
decls.doc: The vertex indexed by the empty subset is the base point.
decls.statement: theorem cubeVertex_empty (x : V → ℤ) : cubeVertex x ∅ = x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_insert
decls.doc:
Adding a direction not already present adds the corresponding basis vector to the cube
vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_insert {T : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∉ T) (x : V → ℤ) :
    cubeVertex x (insert v T) = cubeVertex x T + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_apply
decls.doc:
The coordinate value of a cube vertex. It is `x v + 1` in directions selected by `T`, and
`x v` otherwise.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_apply (x : V → ℤ) (T : Finset V) (v : V) :
    cubeVertex x T v = x v + if v ∈ T then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_add_single_eq_insert
decls.doc:
Shifting the base point by a basis vector `E_v` and adjoining `v` to the directions describe
the same cube vertex, provided `v` was not already a direction.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_add_single_eq_insert {T : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∉ T) (x : V → ℤ) :
    cubeVertex (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) T = cubeVertex x (insert v T)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.single_one_injective
decls.statement: theorem single_one_injective : Function.Injective fun v : V => Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_sum_mem_subsetSum
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_sum_mem_subsetSum {T S : Finset V} (hTS : T ⊆ S) :
    (∑ v ∈ T, Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) ∈
      (S.image fun v => Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)).subsetSum

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices
decls.doc: The finite set of all vertices of the cube with base point `x` and directions `S`.
decls.statement: def cubeVertices (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) : Finset (V → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.mem_cubeVertices
decls.doc:
A point is a vertex of the cube based at `x` with directions `S` exactly when it is
`cubeVertex x T` for some subset `T ⊆ S` of the directions.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_cubeVertices (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (y : V → ℤ) :
    y ∈ cubeVertices x S ↔ ∃ T ⊆ S, cubeVertex x T = y

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.base_mem_cubeVertices
decls.doc: The base point is a vertex of every cube.
decls.statement:
theorem base_mem_cubeVertices (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    x ∈ cubeVertices x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_nonempty
decls.doc: The vertex set of a cube is nonempty.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertices_nonempty (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    (cubeVertices x S).Nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertex_subset_mem_cubeVertices
decls.doc: A direction subset determines a vertex of any cube containing those directions.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertex_subset_mem_cubeVertices {T S : Finset V} (hTS : T ⊆ S) (x : V → ℤ) :
    cubeVertex x T ∈ cubeVertices x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_subset
decls.doc: The vertices of a subcube are vertices of the larger cube.
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertices_subset {S T : Finset V} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : V → ℤ) :
    cubeVertices x S ⊆ cubeVertices x T

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_empty
decls.doc: The zero-dimensional cube has its base point as its only vertex.
decls.statement: theorem cubeVertices_empty (x : V → ℤ) : cubeVertices x ∅ = {x}

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeightValues
decls.doc: The characteristic weight values attained on the vertices of a plumbing cube.
decls.statement:
def characteristicCubeWeightValues
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) : Finset ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeightValues_nonempty
decls.doc: The value set for a plumbing cube is nonempty.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeightValues_nonempty
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    (characteristicCubeWeightValues P k x S).Nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight
decls.doc: The characteristic cube weight is the maximum of the point weights over the cube's vertices.
decls.statement:
def characteristicCubeWeight
  (P : PlumbingGraph V)
  (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_mem_characteristicCubeWeightValues
decls.doc: A vertex weight is one of the values used to form the characteristic cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_mem_characteristicCubeWeightValues
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {y : V → ℤ}
    (hy : y ∈ cubeVertices x S) :
    P.characteristicWeight k y ∈ characteristicCubeWeightValues P k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_le_characteristicCubeWeight
decls.doc: The point weight at any vertex is bounded above by the characteristic cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_le_characteristicCubeWeight
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {y : V → ℤ}
    (hy : y ∈ cubeVertices x S) :
    P.characteristicWeight k y ≤ P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_le
decls.doc: To bound a characteristic cube weight above, bound the weight at every vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_le
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {n : ℤ}
    (h : ∀ y ∈ cubeVertices x S, P.characteristicWeight k y ≤ n) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S ≤ n

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_le_iff
decls.doc: A characteristic cube weight is bounded above by `n` iff every vertex weight is.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_le_iff
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {x : V → ℤ} {S : Finset V} {n : ℤ} :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S ≤ n ↔
      ∀ y ∈ cubeVertices x S, P.characteristicWeight k y ≤ n

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.exists_characteristicWeight_eq_characteristicCubeWeight
decls.doc: The characteristic cube weight is attained at some vertex of the cube.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_characteristicWeight_eq_characteristicCubeWeight
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    ∃ y ∈ cubeVertices x S, P.characteristicWeight k y = P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_cubeVertex_le_characteristicCubeWeight
decls.doc: The point weight at a direction subset is bounded above by the characteristic cube weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_cubeVertex_le_characteristicCubeWeight
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {T S : Finset V} (hTS : T ⊆ S) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (cubeVertex x T) ≤ P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_le_characteristicCubeWeight_base
decls.doc: The base point's weight is bounded above by every cube weight based at that point.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_le_characteristicCubeWeight_base
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    P.characteristicWeight k x ≤ P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_mono
decls.doc: Characteristic cube weight is monotone under enlarging the set of cube directions.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_mono
    (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) {S T : Finset V} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S ≤ P.characteristicCubeWeight k x T

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_empty
decls.doc:
The characteristic cube weight of the zero-dimensional cube is the point weight of its base
point.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_empty (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors)
    (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x ∅ = P.characteristicWeight k x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.cubeVertices_eq_union_erase
decls.doc:
The vertices of a cube split along a direction `v ∈ S` into the vertices of its two faces: a
vertex whose direction subset avoids `v` lies in the lower face (same base point, directions
`S.erase v`), while a vertex whose direction subset contains `v` lies in the upper face (base
point `x + E_v`, directions `S.erase v`).
decls.statement:
theorem cubeVertices_eq_union_erase {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) (x : V → ℤ) :
    cubeVertices x S =
      cubeVertices x (S.erase v) ∪ cubeVertices (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_eq_max_erase
decls.doc:
The cube weight is the maximum of its two face weights in any direction `v ∈ S`: the lower
face (base point `x`, directions `S.erase v`) and the upper face (base point `x + E_v`, directions
`S.erase v`). This is the cubical recursion at the heart of the lattice-homology differential.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_eq_max_erase (x : V → ℤ) {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S =
      max (P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (S.erase v))
        (P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v))

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_insert_eq_max
decls.doc:
The "add a direction" form of the cube-weight recursion: adjoining a new direction `v ∉ S` to
a cube gives the maximum of the original cube weight and the weight of the cube shifted by the new
basis vector `E_v`.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_insert_eq_max (x : V → ℤ) {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∉ S) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (insert v S) =
      max (P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S)
        (P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) S)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.min_characteristicFaceExponent_eq_zero
decls.doc:
In any cube direction `v ∈ S`, at least one of the two face exponents is zero: the cube weight
agrees with the larger of its two face weights, so the difference to that face vanishes. The face
exponents are the `U`-powers of the lattice-homology differential, so in any direction the two
opposite codimension-one faces never both carry a positive `U`-power.
decls.statement:
theorem min_characteristicFaceExponent_eq_zero (x : V → ℤ) {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    min (P.characteristicLowerFaceExponent k x S v)
      (P.characteristicUpperFaceExponent k x S hv) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.sum_adj_mul_le_degree_mul_sq
decls.doc:
The adjacency cross-term sum of the intersection form is bounded above by the degree-weighted
sum of squares: applying `2 (x i)(x j) ≤ (x i)² + (x j)²` on each edge and summing over the two
endpoints turns each edge into a diagonal contribution to both of its endpoints.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_adj_mul_le_degree_mul_sq (x : V → ℤ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then x i * x j else 0) ≤
      ∑ i, (P.toSimpleGraph.degree i : ℤ) * x i ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_self_le_weight_add_degree
decls.doc:
The diagonal-dominance upper bound on the intersection form: the self-pairing is at most the
sum, over spheres, of `(weight i + degree i)` times `(x i)²`. This is the quadratic-form estimate
underlying the negative-definiteness criterion.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_self_le_weight_add_degree (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm x x ≤
      ∑ i, (P.weight i + P.toSimpleGraph.degree i) * x i ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isNegativeDefinite_of_degree_lt_neg_weight
decls.doc:
**Strict diagonal dominance implies negative-definiteness.** If every sphere's framing is more
negative than its number of neighbours, `degree i < - weight i`, then the plumbing is negative
definite.

The row-sum condition makes each coefficient `weight i + degree i` strictly negative, so the
diagonal-dominance bound `intersectionForm_self_le_weight_add_degree` expresses `x · x` as at most
a sum of nonpositive terms; picking a coordinate where `x` is nonzero makes that sum strictly
negative.
decls.title: Strict diagonal dominance implies negative-definiteness
decls.statement:
theorem isNegativeDefinite_of_degree_lt_neg_weight
    (h : ∀ i, (P.toSimpleGraph.degree i : ℤ) < -P.weight i) : P.IsNegativeDefinite

decls.name: TauCeti.triangleMinusThreePlumbing
decls.doc:
The triangle plumbing on three spheres, each with framing `-3`: its underlying graph is the
complete graph `K₃`, so every vertex has degree `2`, and `2 < 3`. A self-validating instance of
the diagonal-dominance criterion whose graph carries edges (so the adjacency bound is genuinely
used), where hand square-completion would be more laborious than for `A₂`.
decls.statement: def triangleMinusThreePlumbing : PlumbingGraph (Fin 3)

decls.name: TauCeti.triangleMinusThreePlumbing_degree
decls.statement:
theorem triangleMinusThreePlumbing_degree (i : Fin 3) :
    triangleMinusThreePlumbing.toSimpleGraph.degree i = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingCoefficient
decls.doc: The coefficient ring for the first, characteristic-two lattice-homology complex.
decls.statement: abbrev PlumbingCoefficient

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingChain
decls.doc: The free `𝔽₂[U]`-module generated by plumbing-lattice cubes.
decls.statement: abbrev PlumbingChain (V : Type*)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferentialOnGenerator
decls.doc:
The lattice differential of one plumbing-cube generator.

For every direction of the cube, this is the sum of its lower and upper faces weighted by the
drop in characteristic cube weight.
decls.statement:
def latticeDifferentialOnGenerator
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    PlumbingChain V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferentialOnGenerator_def
decls.doc: The defining weighted face-sum formula for the generator differential.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferentialOnGenerator_def
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    P.latticeDifferentialOnGenerator k C =
      C.directions.attach.sum fun v =>
        Finsupp.single (C.lowerFace v v.property)
            (Polynomial.X ^ PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v) +
          Finsupp.single (C.upperFace v v.property)
            (Polynomial.X ^ PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C v.property)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential
decls.doc: The `𝔽₂[U]`-linear lattice differential on plumbing chains.
decls.statement:
def latticeDifferential
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    PlumbingChain V →ₗ[PlumbingCoefficient] PlumbingChain V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_single
decls.doc:
The lattice differential sends a single cube with coefficient `a` to `a` times its weighted
sum of codimension-one faces.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_single
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V)
    (a : PlumbingCoefficient) :
    (@latticeDifferential V decV finV P k)
        (Finsupp.single C a) =
      a • @latticeDifferentialOnGenerator V decV finV P k C

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_apply
decls.doc:
The lattice differential is the finite linear combination of its values on the generators
in the support of a chain.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_apply
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (c : PlumbingChain V) :
    (@latticeDifferential V decV finV P k) c =
      c.sum fun C a => a • @latticeDifferentialOnGenerator V decV finV P k C

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.lowerFaceDirectionEquiv
decls.doc:
Reindex the directions of a lower face by the ambient directions other than the removed
one.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.upperFaceDirectionEquiv
decls.doc:
Reindex the directions of an upper face by the ambient directions other than the removed
one.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.directionPairEquiv
decls.doc:
Identify a direction followed by a remaining direction with an ordered pair of distinct
ambient directions.
decls.statement:
def directionPairEquiv (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    (Σ v : C.directions, C.directions.erase v) ≃ C.directions.offDiag

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferentialTwoDirections
decls.doc:
The four terms obtained by taking two faces in the ordered pair of distinct directions
recorded by `p`. This is the summand paired with the reversed direction pair in the proof that
the differential squares to zero.
decls.statement:
def latticeDifferentialTwoDirections
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V)
    (p : {p // p ∈ C.directions.offDiag}) : PlumbingChain V

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.swapOffDiag
decls.doc: Reversing an ordered off-diagonal pair of cube directions.

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferentialTwoDirections_swap
decls.doc:
Reversing the two directions leaves the total four-face contribution unchanged. The
lower-lower and upper-upper terms match their counterparts, while the two mixed terms are
exchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferentialTwoDirections_swap
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V)
    (p : {p // p ∈ C.directions.offDiag}) :
    latticeDifferentialTwoDirections P k C (swapOffDiag C p) =
      latticeDifferentialTwoDirections P k C p

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.sum_latticeDifferentialTwoDirections_eq_zero
decls.doc:
The total contribution over ordered pairs of distinct directions vanishes in characteristic
two: pair `(v, w)` with `(w, v)`.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_latticeDifferentialTwoDirections_eq_zero
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    C.directions.offDiag.attach.sum
        (latticeDifferentialTwoDirections P k C) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_latticeDifferentialOnGenerator
decls.doc:
Expanding the differential twice on a cube gives the sum of the four-face contributions over
ordered pairs of distinct directions.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_latticeDifferentialOnGenerator
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    P.latticeDifferential k (P.latticeDifferentialOnGenerator k C) =
      C.directions.offDiag.attach.sum
        (latticeDifferentialTwoDirections P k C)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_latticeDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero
decls.doc: The differential of the weighted boundary of a single plumbing cube vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_latticeDifferentialOnGenerator_eq_zero
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    P.latticeDifferential k (P.latticeDifferentialOnGenerator k C) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_comp_self
decls.doc: The characteristic-two weighted lattice differential squares to zero.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_comp_self
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    (P.latticeDifferential k).comp (P.latticeDifferential k) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeDifferential_eq_zero_of_isEmpty
decls.doc:
The lattice differential vanishes when the plumbing graph has no vertices. Every cube then
has an empty direction set, so the weighted face sum on every generator is empty.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeDifferential_eq_zero_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty V]
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.latticeDifferential k = 0
