decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing
decls.doc:
The `E₈` plumbing: a chain of seven `-2`-framed vertices, with one further `-2`-framed
vertex attached to the third vertex of the chain.
decls.statement: def e8Plumbing : PlumbingGraph (Fin 8)

decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing_weight
decls.doc: Every vertex of the `E₈` plumbing has framing `-2`.
decls.statement: theorem e8Plumbing_weight (i : Fin 8) : e8Plumbing.weight i = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing_adj
decls.doc:
Two vertices of the `E₈` plumbing are adjacent exactly when they are one of the seven
unordered pairs in its Dynkin tree.

decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing_intersectionForm_self
decls.doc:
The self-intersection of a vector in the `E₈` plumbing lattice, expanded along the seven
edges of the Dynkin tree.
decls.statement:
theorem e8Plumbing_intersectionForm_self (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8Plumbing.intersectionForm x x =
      -2 * ∑ i, x i ^ 2 +
        2 * (x 0 * x 1 + x 1 * x 2 + x 2 * x 3 + x 3 * x 4 +
          x 4 * x 5 + x 5 * x 6 + x 2 * x 7)

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm
decls.doc:
The eight nonnegative square terms in the integral completion of squares for the `E₈`
intersection form.
decls.statement: def e8SquareTerm (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) : Fin 8 → ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_zero (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 0 = 420 * (2 * x 0 - x 1) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_one
decls.doc: The first completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_one (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 1 = 140 * (3 * x 1 - 2 * x 2) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_two
decls.doc: The second completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_two (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 2 = 70 * (4 * x 2 - 3 * x 3 - 3 * x 7) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_three
decls.doc: The third completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_three (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 3 = 42 * (5 * x 3 - 4 * x 4 - 3 * x 7) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_four
decls.doc: The fourth completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_four (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 4 = 28 * (6 * x 4 - 5 * x 5 - 3 * x 7) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_five
decls.doc: The fifth completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_five (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 5 = 20 * (7 * x 5 - 6 * x 6 - 3 * x 7) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_six
decls.doc: The sixth completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_six (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 6 = 15 * (8 * x 6 - 3 * x 7) ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_seven
decls.doc: The seventh completed-square term.
decls.statement:
theorem e8SquareTerm_seven (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    e8SquareTerm x 7 = 105 * x 7 ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.e8SquareTerm_nonneg
decls.doc: Every term in the completed-square expression for `E₈` is nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem e8SquareTerm_nonneg (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) (i : Fin 8) : 0 ≤ e8SquareTerm x i

decls.name: TauCeti.eq_zero_of_e8SquareTerm_sum_eq_zero
decls.doc: The completed-square expression for `E₈` vanishes only at the zero vector.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_e8SquareTerm_sum_eq_zero (x : Fin 8 → ℤ)
    (h : ∑ i, e8SquareTerm x i = 0) :
    x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing_neg_intersectionForm
decls.doc:
An integral completion of squares for the negative `E₈` intersection form. Multiplication by
`840` clears the denominators in the usual `LDLᵀ` decomposition of the `E₈` Cartan matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem e8Plumbing_neg_intersectionForm (x : Fin 8 → ℤ) :
    -840 * e8Plumbing.intersectionForm x x = ∑ i, e8SquareTerm x i

decls.name: TauCeti.e8Plumbing_isNegativeDefinite
decls.doc: The `E₈` plumbing is negative definite.
decls.statement: theorem e8Plumbing_isNegativeDefinite : e8Plumbing.IsNegativeDefinite

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex
decls.doc:
The short complex whose two maps are the characteristic-two lattice differential.

The three objects are the total plumbing-chain module on all cubical dimensions. The short-complex
condition is exactly `latticeDifferential_comp_self`.
decls.statement:
def latticeShortComplex
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    ShortComplex (ModuleCat PlumbingCoefficient)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex_X₁
decls.doc: The left object of the lattice short complex is the plumbing-chain module.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeShortComplex_X₁ (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    (P.latticeShortComplex k).X₁ =
      ModuleCat.of PlumbingCoefficient (PlumbingChain V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex_X₂
decls.doc: The middle object of the lattice short complex is the plumbing-chain module.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeShortComplex_X₂ (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    (P.latticeShortComplex k).X₂ =
      ModuleCat.of PlumbingCoefficient (PlumbingChain V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex_X₃
decls.doc: The right object of the lattice short complex is the plumbing-chain module.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeShortComplex_X₃ (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    (P.latticeShortComplex k).X₃ =
      ModuleCat.of PlumbingCoefficient (PlumbingChain V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex_f
decls.doc: The left map of the lattice short complex is the lattice differential.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeShortComplex_f (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    HEq (P.latticeShortComplex k).f
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (P.latticeDifferential k))

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeShortComplex_g
decls.doc: The right map of the lattice short complex is the lattice differential.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeShortComplex_g (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    HEq (P.latticeShortComplex k).g
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (P.latticeDifferential k))

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeHomology
decls.doc:
The characteristic-two lattice homology module: the homology of the weighted
plumbing-lattice short complex.

This is Mathlib's canonical homology object, so the generic `ShortComplex.cycles`,
`ShortComplex.homologyπ`, and homology-map API can be used directly via `latticeHomology_def`.
decls.statement:
def latticeHomology
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) : ModuleCat PlumbingCoefficient

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeHomology_def
decls.doc: Lattice homology is the canonical homology object of the lattice short complex.
decls.statement:
theorem latticeHomology_def (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.latticeHomology k = (P.latticeShortComplex k).homology

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeHomologyIsoChainOfIsEmpty
decls.doc:
The characteristic-two lattice homology of a zero-vertex plumbing is canonically isomorphic
to its whole plumbing-chain module.
decls.statement:
def latticeHomologyIsoChainOfIsEmpty [IsEmpty V]
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.latticeHomology k ≅ ModuleCat.of PlumbingCoefficient (PlumbingChain V)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeHomologyIsoCoefficientOfIsEmpty
decls.doc:
The characteristic-two lattice homology of a zero-vertex plumbing is a universe-lifted copy
of the coefficient module `𝔽₂[U]`.
decls.statement:
def latticeHomologyIsoCoefficientOfIsEmpty [IsEmpty V]
    (P : PlumbingGraph V) (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.latticeHomology k ≅
      ModuleCat.of PlumbingCoefficient (ULift.{u} PlumbingCoefficient)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph
decls.doc:
A plumbing graph: a simple graph together with an integer weight on each vertex.

The vertices are the plumbed spheres, the edges record which pairs of spheres are plumbed
together, and `weight v` is the self-intersection number (the framing / Euler number) of the
sphere `v`. The combinatorics is modelled by a `SimpleGraph`: at most one edge between two
distinct vertices, and no self-loops. The finite lattice API is provided by declarations that
assume `[Fintype V]`.
decls.statement: structure PlumbingGraph (V : Type*)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix
decls.doc:
The intersection matrix of a plumbing graph: the framing on the diagonal and the adjacency
indicator off the diagonal.

This is the matrix of the intersection form of the plumbed four-manifold in the basis of
spheres: a sphere meets itself in its framing and meets a plumbed neighbour once.
decls.statement: def intersectionMatrix : Matrix V V ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_apply
decls.doc:
The entry of the intersection matrix: the framing when on the diagonal plus one for each
adjacency.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionMatrix_apply (i j : V) :
    P.intersectionMatrix i j =
      (if i = j then P.weight i else 0) + (if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then 1 else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_diag
decls.doc:
The diagonal entry of the intersection matrix is the framing: a sphere has no self-loop, so
the adjacency term vanishes.
decls.statement: theorem intersectionMatrix_diag (i : V) : P.intersectionMatrix i i = P.weight i

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_apply_of_ne
decls.doc: Off the diagonal the intersection matrix is the adjacency indicator.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionMatrix_apply_of_ne {i j : V} (h : i ≠ j) :
    P.intersectionMatrix i j = if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_of_adj
decls.doc: Two plumbed spheres meet once: an adjacency contributes the entry one.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionMatrix_of_adj {i j : V} (h : P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j) :
    P.intersectionMatrix i j = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_of_not_adj
decls.doc: Distinct non-adjacent spheres are disjoint: the entry is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionMatrix_of_not_adj {i j : V} (hij : i ≠ j) (h : ¬ P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j) :
    P.intersectionMatrix i j = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionMatrix_isSymm
decls.doc:
The intersection matrix is symmetric: the diagonal framing matrix and the adjacency matrix
are each symmetric.
decls.statement: theorem intersectionMatrix_isSymm : P.intersectionMatrix.IsSymm

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite
decls.doc:
A plumbing graph is **negative definite** when its intersection matrix is negative
definite, equivalently when the negated intersection matrix is positive definite. For finite
plumbed three-manifolds this is the standing hypothesis under which lattice homology computes
the Heegaard Floer invariant.
decls.statement: def IsNegativeDefinite : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isNegativeDefinite_iff
decls.doc: The defining matrix characterization of a negative-definite plumbing graph.
decls.statement: theorem isNegativeDefinite_iff : P.IsNegativeDefinite ↔ (-P.intersectionMatrix).PosDef

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.weight_neg
decls.doc:
A negative-definite plumbing graph has every framing negative: a diagonal entry of the
positive-definite negated intersection matrix is the negated framing.
decls.statement: theorem IsNegativeDefinite.weight_neg (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) (i : V) : P.weight i < 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm
decls.doc:
The intersection form of a plumbing graph: the symmetric `ℤ`-bilinear form on `V → ℤ` with
matrix `intersectionMatrix`.
decls.statement: def intersectionForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ (V → ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_apply
decls.doc: The intersection form expanded as a double sum over the intersection matrix entries.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_apply (x y : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm x y = ∑ i, ∑ j, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i j * y j

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_single
decls.doc: The intersection form pairs the basis sphere classes by the intersection matrix entries.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_single (i j : V) :
    P.intersectionForm (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1) = P.intersectionMatrix i j

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_isSymm
decls.doc: The intersection form is symmetric.
decls.statement: theorem intersectionForm_isSymm : P.intersectionForm.IsSymm

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_self_add
decls.doc:
The intersection form on a sum expands by the symmetric polarization: the cross term appears
twice because the form is symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_self_add (x y : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm (x + y) (x + y) =
      P.intersectionForm x x + 2 * P.intersectionForm x y + P.intersectionForm y y

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_single_right
decls.doc:
The intersection pairing of a lattice point against a basis sphere is the corresponding column
sum of the intersection matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_single_right (x : V → ℤ) (v : V) :
    P.intersectionForm x (Pi.single v 1) = ∑ i, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.sum_intersectionMatrix_mulVec_mul
decls.doc:
The linear pairing of the covector `A m` against a lattice point `x` is the intersection
pairing `A(x, m)`: summing `intersectionMatrix.mulVec m` against `x` is the dot product
`(A m) ⬝ᵥ x`, which the symmetry of the dot product turns into the bilinear form `A(x, m)`.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_intersectionMatrix_mulVec_mul (m x : V → ℤ) :
    ∑ v, (P.intersectionMatrix.mulVec m) v * x v = P.intersectionForm x m

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_sum_single_right
decls.doc:
The intersection pairing of a lattice point against a finite sum of basis spheres, as a sum of
the individual column sums.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_sum_single_right (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) :
    P.intersectionForm x (∑ v ∈ S, Pi.single v 1) =
      ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ i, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_sum_single_self
decls.doc:
The self-pairing of a finite sum of basis spheres is the double sum of the intersection-matrix
entries over the chosen directions.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_sum_single_self (S : Finset V) :
    P.intersectionForm (∑ v ∈ S, Pi.single v 1) (∑ w ∈ S, Pi.single w 1) =
      ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ S, P.intersectionMatrix v w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_apply_weight_add_adj
decls.doc: The intersection form expanded into its framing contribution and adjacency contribution.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_apply_weight_add_adj (x y : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm x y =
      (∑ i, P.weight i * x i * y i) +
        ∑ i, ∑ j, if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then x i * y j else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.intersectionForm_self
decls.doc:
The intersection form as a quadratic form: its value on a single class is the
framing-weighted sum of squares together with the adjacency cross terms.
decls.statement:
theorem intersectionForm_self (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm x x =
      (∑ i, P.weight i * x i ^ 2) +
        ∑ i, ∑ j, if P.toSimpleGraph.Adj i j then x i * x j else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.a2Plumbing
decls.doc:
The two-vertex plumbing with a single edge and both framings `-2`: the `A₂` plumbing, whose
intersection form is the negative of the `A₂` Cartan matrix. A self-validating example for the
entry formulas.
decls.statement: def a2Plumbing : PlumbingGraph (Fin 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.a2Plumbing_intersectionMatrix
decls.doc: The intersection matrix of the `A₂` plumbing is the standard `[-2, 1; 1, -2]` matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem a2Plumbing_intersectionMatrix :
    a2Plumbing.intersectionMatrix = !![(-2 : ℤ), 1; 1, -2]

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_neg
decls.doc:
On a negative-definite plumbing the intersection form is strictly negative on every nonzero
lattice vector: the defining inequality `0 < xᵀ (-A) x` of the negated matrix is exactly
`P.intersectionForm x x < 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_neg (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) {x : V → ℤ}
    (hx : x ≠ 0) : P.intersectionForm x x < 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.isNegativeDefinite_iff_forall_intersectionForm_self_neg
decls.doc:
A plumbing is negative definite exactly when its intersection-form self-pairing is strictly
negative on every nonzero lattice vector.
decls.statement:
theorem isNegativeDefinite_iff_forall_intersectionForm_self_neg :
    P.IsNegativeDefinite ↔ ∀ x : V → ℤ, x ≠ 0 → P.intersectionForm x x < 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_nonpos
decls.doc:
On a negative-definite plumbing the intersection form self-pairing is always nonpositive: it
is strictly negative away from the origin and zero at it.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_nonpos (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.intersectionForm x x ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
On a negative-definite plumbing the intersection form self-pairing vanishes exactly at the
origin: negative-definiteness rules out nonzero isotropic vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_self_eq_zero_iff (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite)
    (x : V → ℤ) : P.intersectionForm x x = 0 ↔ x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate
decls.doc:
The intersection form of a negative-definite plumbing is nondegenerate: a lattice vector that
pairs to zero with every vector — in particular with itself — is zero, on either side.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) :
    P.intersectionForm.Nondegenerate

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.eq_zero_of_intersectionForm_left
decls.doc:
A left-kernel form of `IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate`: a lattice vector
pairing to zero with every vector is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.eq_zero_of_intersectionForm_left (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) {x : V → ℤ}
    (hx : ∀ y, P.intersectionForm x y = 0) : x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.eq_zero_of_intersectionForm_right
decls.doc:
A right-kernel form of `IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate`: a lattice vector
paired to zero by every vector is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.eq_zero_of_intersectionForm_right (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite)
    {x : V → ℤ} (hx : ∀ y, P.intersectionForm y x = 0) : x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.mulVec_injective
decls.doc:
On a negative-definite plumbing, multiplication by the intersection matrix is injective: the
lattice embeds along its intersection form, with no kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNegativeDefinite.mulVec_injective (h : P.IsNegativeDefinite) :
    Function.Injective (P.intersectionMatrix *ᵥ ·)

decls.name: TauCeti.a2Plumbing_isNegativeDefinite
decls.doc:
The `A₂` plumbing is negative definite: its negated intersection matrix is the `A₂` Cartan
matrix `!![2, -1; -1, 2]`, whose quadratic form `2x₀² - 2x₀x₁ + 2x₁² = (x₀ - x₁)² + x₀² + x₁²` is
positive on every nonzero integer vector. A self-validating instance of the negative-definite
hypothesis used in Lane L.
decls.statement: theorem a2Plumbing_isNegativeDefinite : a2Plumbing.IsNegativeDefinite

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator
decls.doc:
The numerator of the characteristic weight function:
`⟨k, x⟩ + x · x`, where `x · x` is the plumbing intersection form. For a characteristic covector
`k`, this numerator is even; see `even_characteristicWeightNumerator`.
decls.statement: def characteristicWeightNumerator (k x : V → ℤ) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_def_aux
decls.doc: The numerator of the characteristic weight function, expanded as the defining sum.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_def_aux (k x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x = (∑ v, k v * x v) + P.intersectionForm x x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_def
decls.doc: The numerator of the characteristic weight function, expanded as the defining sum.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_def (k x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x = (∑ v, k v * x v) + P.intersectionForm x x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.even_characteristicWeightNumerator
decls.doc:
The characteristic-weight numerator is even when `k` is characteristic. This is the
integer-valuedness input for the lattice-homology weight function.
decls.statement:
theorem even_characteristicWeightNumerator {k : V → ℤ} (hk : P.IsCharacteristicVector k)
    (x : V → ℤ) : Even (P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight
decls.doc:
The characteristic-weight expression obtained by integer-dividing
`-(⟨k, x⟩ + x · x)` by `2`. For a characteristic covector, the numerator is even by
`even_characteristicWeightNumerator`, and `two_mul_characteristicWeight` states its exact
doubling equation.
decls.statement: def characteristicWeight (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_def_aux
decls.doc: The characteristic weight as the negative half of its numerator.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_def_aux (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight k x = -(P.characteristicWeightNumerator k.val x / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_def
decls.doc: The characteristic weight as the negative half of its numerator.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_def (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight k x = -(P.characteristicWeightNumerator k.val x / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.two_mul_characteristicWeight
decls.doc: The defining equation for the integer-valued characteristic weight.
decls.statement:
theorem two_mul_characteristicWeight (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) :
    2 * P.characteristicWeight k x = -P.characteristicWeightNumerator k.val x

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_zero
decls.doc: The characteristic weight at the zero lattice point is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_zero (k : P.characteristicVectors) :
    P.characteristicWeight k 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_add
decls.doc:
The numerator is additive in its covector argument: shifting `k` by `l` adds the linear
pairing `⟨l, x⟩`.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_add (k l x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator (fun v => k v + l v) x =
      P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x + ∑ v, l v * x v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_add_two_mul
decls.doc: The numerator for a covector shifted by twice another covector.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_add_two_mul (k l x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator (fun v => k v + 2 * l v) x =
      P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x + 2 * ∑ v, l v * x v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add_two_mul
decls.doc:
Shifting a covector by `2l` subtracts the linear pairing `⟨l, x⟩` from the
characteristic weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add_two_mul (k : P.characteristicVectors) (l x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight ⟨fun v => k.val v + 2 * l v, k.property.add_two_mul⟩ x =
      P.characteristicWeight k x - ∑ v, l v * x v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_single
decls.doc:
The numerator of any covector on a plumbing basis sphere is the covector coordinate plus the
sphere weight.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_single (k : V → ℤ) (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator k (Pi.single v 1) = k v + P.weight v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_canonical_single
decls.doc: The numerator of the canonical characteristic covector on a basis sphere is `-2`.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_canonical_single (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator P.canonicalCharacteristic (Pi.single v 1) = -2

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_single
decls.doc: The characteristic weight of any characteristic covector on a plumbing basis sphere.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_single (k : P.characteristicVectors) (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (Pi.single v 1) = -((k.val v + P.weight v) / 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_canonical_single
decls.doc: The canonical characteristic covector has characteristic weight `1` on each basis sphere.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_canonical_single (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeight
      ⟨P.canonicalCharacteristic, P.isCharacteristicVector_canonicalCharacteristic⟩
      (Pi.single v 1) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeightNumerator_add_right
decls.doc:
The characteristic-weight numerator is quadratic in the lattice point: on a sum it gains twice
the intersection pairing of the two summands.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeightNumerator_add_right (k x y : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeightNumerator k (x + y) =
      P.characteristicWeightNumerator k x + P.characteristicWeightNumerator k y +
        2 * P.intersectionForm x y

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add
decls.doc:
The polarization identity for Némethi's weight function: `χ_k` is quadratic, with associated
symmetric bilinear form the negated intersection form.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x y : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (x + y) =
      P.characteristicWeight k x + P.characteristicWeight k y - P.intersectionForm x y

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add_single
decls.doc:
The first-difference recursion of `χ_k` along a basis direction: taking one lattice step in the
direction `v` subtracts `(k_v + weight v) / 2` and the pairing of the current point against the
`v`-th sphere. This is the step that drives the cube-weight comparisons of lattice homology.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add_single (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (v : V) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (x + Pi.single v 1) =
      P.characteristicWeight k x - ((k.val v + P.weight v) / 2) -
        ∑ i, x i * P.intersectionMatrix i v

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_single_add_single
decls.doc:
The value of `χ_k` on a sum of two basis spheres, with the interaction term given by their
intersection-matrix entry: for adjacent spheres this entry is `1`, otherwise `0` off-diagonal.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_single_add_single (k : P.characteristicVectors) (v w : V) :
    P.characteristicWeight k (Pi.single v 1 + Pi.single w 1) =
      P.characteristicWeight k (Pi.single v 1) + P.characteristicWeight k (Pi.single w 1) -
        P.intersectionMatrix v w

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec
decls.doc:
Shifting a characteristic covector by `2 · A l`, the covector representing the same spin^c
structure translated by `l`, subtracts the intersection pairing `A(x, l)` from the weight. This is
the covector-shift half of the translation equivariance.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec (k : P.characteristicVectors) (m x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight
        ⟨fun v => k.val v + 2 * (P.intersectionMatrix.mulVec m) v, k.property.add_two_mul⟩ x =
      P.characteristicWeight k x - P.intersectionForm x m

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec_eq_sub
decls.doc:
Spin^c translation equivariance of Némethi's weight function: shifting the characteristic
covector by `2 · A l` translates the weight by `l`, up to the additive constant `χ_k(l)`,

`χ_{k + 2·A l}(x) = χ_k(x + l) - χ_k(l)`.

The two representatives `k` and `k + 2·A l` of one spin^c structure therefore have weight functions
that agree after translating the lattice argument by `l`; this is the weight-level statement behind
the translation isomorphism of the associated lattice homologies.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec_eq_sub (k : P.characteristicVectors) (m x : V → ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight
        ⟨fun v => k.val v + 2 * (P.intersectionMatrix.mulVec m) v, k.property.add_two_mul⟩ x =
      P.characteristicWeight k (x + m) - P.characteristicWeight k m

decls.name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec_le_iff
decls.doc:
The sublevel sets of two spin^c representatives correspond under the `l`-translation, with a
constant grading shift by `χ_k(l)`: a point `x` has shifted-covector weight at most `n` exactly when
its `l`-translate has original weight at most `n + χ_k(l)`. This is the degree-preserving bijection
of cubical generators underlying the spin^c invariance of lattice homology.
decls.statement:
theorem characteristicWeight_add_two_mulVec_le_iff (k : P.characteristicVectors) (m x : V → ℤ)
    (n : ℤ) :
    P.characteristicWeight
        ⟨fun v => k.val v + 2 * (P.intersectionMatrix.mulVec m) v, k.property.add_two_mul⟩ x ≤ n ↔
      P.characteristicWeight k (x + m) ≤ n + P.characteristicWeight k m
